papers.title: Effect of Gas Pressure and Molecular Structure in the Spatial-Mode Conversion of Terahertz Radiation from a Plasma Filament
papers.abstract: In this work, the generation of terahertz (THz) radiation under single color filamentation of a femtosecond laser pulse in an optical cell with compressed gases (argon, nitrogen, CO2) in broad pressure range from 0.001 to 25 atm is experimentally studied for the first time. A nonmonotonic dependence of the integral energy of the THz signal on the gas pressure is revealed, which can be attributed to the competition between an increase in the plasma density and the development of plasma selfabsorption processes, multiple filamentation of the femtosecond pump, and collision induced absorption in the neutral medium. We show that the molecular structure of the gas critically determines the pressure optimum of generation, shifting the maximum of the THz energy yield to the region of elevated pressures (from 10 to 15 atm) for monatomic argon and to the region of subatmospheric pressures (approx. 0.1 atm) for molecular carbon dioxide due to strong vibrational rotational dissipation. On the basis of numerical 3D modeling, it is shown that the cylindrical metal waveguide insert used for signal collection operates in a strongly multimode regime and substantially transforms the angular spectrum of the THz source. We demonstrate that the conical structure of the THz radiation recorded in the experiment is a consequence of intermode interference and diffraction at the output end face of the waveguide, which transforms the true parameters of THz generation in the plasma channel.

papers.title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
papers.abstract: Opacity of mid- and high-$Z$ plasmas is dominated by thousands of overlapping spectral lines. Examples are laser-produced plasmas for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, inertial-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors. Radiation transport in such plasmas needs more than 1000 photon-energy groups in the EUV case, and this makes radiation-hydrodynamic simulations very expensive. We show that the accuracy of a small-group opacity model can be recovered by choosing properly \emph{which} fine bins are put into the same group. We present a data-driven method that assigns the fine bins of a detailed opacity and emissivity table to $K$ \emph{non-contiguous} groups. Each group has a fixed spectral shape inside it. The groups follow from one requirement: the reduced absorption operator must be diagonal for every plasma state. They are determined from a Gram matrix of spectra, taken from detailed-group solutions of a small part, for example 5\% in this work, of the parameter space. The reduced model is a set of $K$ uncoupled flux-limited diffusion equations. It can be used in an existing multigroup code by replacing the opacity table. For a Sn plasma with electron densities of $4\times10^{15}$--$1.1\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-3}$, electron temperatures of 5--250~eV, and scale lengths of 2.5--6900$\um$, the model with $K=100$ reproduces the total flux of the 1500-group reference with a median error of 2\% and a 90th-percentile error of 8\%. The 90th-percentile error is ten times smaller than that of a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.

papers.title: Multi-dimensional kinetic modeling of laser-plasma instabilities by a Vlasov-Maxwell system
papers.abstract: We present PLAW-EM2d (Two-Dimensional PLAsmaWave ElectroMagnetic Simulation), a two-dimensional Vlasov-Maxwell code for kinetic studies of laser-plasma interactions. The code combines a hybrid electrostatic- TEz field decomposition with an Eulerian 2d2v Vlasov solver for the electron distribution function and a cold closure for the out-of-plane response. Vacuum propagation, Landau damping, and a homogeneousplasma comparison with PIC simulations benchmark the coupled solver. We then consider two representative SRS problems. In an inhomogeneous plasma, the code reproduces convective SRS backscatter with a reflectivity consistent with the Rosenbluth estimate. In a transversely extended target, it captures SRS side scattering in a self-consistent two-dimensional Vlasov simulation, resolving oblique electromagnetic and Langmuir waves that satisfy the resonance conditions. These calculations show that PLAW-EM2d can describe both conventional SRS backscatter and a two-dimensional side-scattering channel relevant to laser-plasma interactions in ICF.

papers.title: Cross-channel amplification of frequency-distinct scattered waves in multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering
papers.abstract: Multibeam stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) can be amplified when one side-scattered wave draws energy from several pumps, each through a separate ion-acoustic-wave (IAW) branch. This is not common-daughter-wave coupling: scattered waves from different parent pumps may occupy nearly the same wave-vector region yet remain distinct optical modes because their frequencies differ. We examine this process with local-growth and finite-width-gain models, three-dimensional coupled-mode calculations and two-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. Adding the extra branches increases temporal growth and spatial gain across the tested crossing angles. In three dimensions, direct branches alone give weak, localized side scatter; with the cross branches present, a strong field fills much of the interaction region even though the incident beams, direct channels and initial seed are unchanged. The distinction persists at fixed total power. The coupled response remains strong as the power per beam falls, whereas the direct-only response drops rapidly. PIC spectra contain nearby scattered-light features accompanied by several pump-specific IAW branches, and the fixed-power scans yield a strong, non-monotonic response. These results support cross-channel feedback through separate IAWs as a multibeam SBS amplification mechanism that may help predict and control SBS losses in laser-fusion plasmas.

papers.title: Impurity turbulent transport and its role in driving zonal flows in tokamak plasmas
papers.abstract: The driving mechanisms of zonal flows (ZFs) in multi-ion-species tokamak plasmas are investigated by using gyrokinetic theory and simulations. For deuterium plasmas containing either helium ash with a steep density gradient or lithium impurity at a high charge concentration, the magnitude of impurity turbulent energy flux (TEF) can be comparable to, or even stronger than, that of the main-ion TEF. Moreover, the impurity TEF significantly drives ZFs. Both the impurity and main-ion turbulent poloidal Reynolds stress (PRS) drives are significant for the case with a high lithium charge concentration. The shielding timescale of the turbulent PRS drive is found to be the damping time of geodesic acoustic mode, which is significantly shorter than one ion bounce period.

papers.title: SFQED Cascade Saturation and Laser Depletion Dynamics In CP Rotating Laser Standing Waves
papers.abstract: Multi-petawatt laser facilities are approaching the regime where colliding laser pulses can spontaneously ignite self-sustained QED cascades, converting laser energy into dense electron-positron plasmas. Using 1D PIC-QED simulations of a circularly polarized standing wave, we characterize the complete lifecycle of seeded cascades from exponential growth through relativistic opacity and macroscopic laser depletion. We show that cascade saturation is governed by the competition between pair creation and longitudinal lepton migration out of the magnetic nodes. The overdense plasma reflects the driving laser, disrupting the standing wave and triggering secondary cascades in adjacent nodes, driving an apparent spatial expansion whose velocity scales linearly with the cascade growth rate. Finally, we generalize an analytical laser absorption model to realistic time-dependent pulse envelopes, accurately reproducing the simulated conversion efficiency of laser energy into gamma-ray photons and electron-positron pairs.

papers.title: Laser-Driven Electron Stripping from Nanoparticles in Plasma
papers.abstract: Laser wakefield accelerators use plasma wake waves to produce high-energy electron beams over short distances. Nanoparticles can trigger localized electron injection, with their size and density influencing the accelerated beam charge. However, the electron charge of a nanoparticle does not determine how much charge is stripped by the laser. Here we show that a quasistatic electrostatic model predicts laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles, in agreement with particle-in-cell simulations in vacuum and helium plasma. The model identifies a saturation density that increases with laser amplitude and decreases with nanoparticle radius, separating complete from partial stripping. Above this density, the stripped electron fraction decreases and the stripped charge approaches a finite limit. Multicycle pulses produce more stripped charge than the model predicts due to time-dependent electron dynamics. In helium plasma, plasma wake waves induce additional electron stripping. These results give an understanding of the scaling of laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles and could inform nanoparticle parameter selection for future nanoparticle-assisted laser wakefield accelerators.

papers.title: Impact of edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation on L-H transition in the KSTAR tokamak
papers.abstract: The impact of edge-localized resonant magnetic perturbation (ERMP) on the low-to-high (L-H) confinement mode transition is investigated through dedicated experiments on the KSTAR tokamak with tungsten divertor and numerical simulations with a one-dimensional (1D) reduced transport model. Experimentally, under matched conditions, the ERMP inhibits the L-H transition, whereas the reference discharge without ERMP enters H-mode. The ERMP enhances edge electron temperature fluctuations and the turbulence decorrelation rate, and flattens the toroidal rotation, reducing the edge $E\times B$ velocity shear below the threshold required for turbulence suppression. An extended 1D predator-prey model, which incorporates toroidal flow evolution and realistic radial profile of the magnetic perturbation due to plasma response field, reproduces the experimental trends of enhanced turbulence, reduced ExB flow shear, and inhibited L-H transition. These findings contribute to a better understanding of how ERMP affects L-H transition dynamics in tungsten divertor environments and offer a valuable reference for the application of ERMP in current and future fusion devices.

papers.title: Self-consistent thermal-runaway electron equilibria
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop and solve a self-consistent equilibrium model for plasmas containing thermal and runaway electron (RE) populations, motivated by observations of residual plasma density during alternating-current (AC) transitions in ISTTOK. We adopt an existing monoenergetic, narrow-pitch guiding-center formulation, while retaining a spatially varying toroidal-field function, and show that prescribing the radius-weighted RE density by the orbit label alone conflicts with particle conservation and vector equilibrium wherever the thermal toroidal-field function varies along an occupied drift contour. Both conditions instead require the ratio of RE density to toroidal field to be constant along each drift contour. Taking this ratio as a function of the orbit label gives a compatible closure that relates the equilibrium RE density to a prescribed reference profile. Combined with Grad-Shafranov-Helmholtz thermal free functions, it yields a closed field equation that retains the displacement between drift and magnetic surfaces. At fixed thermal coefficients, we prove existence for every finite reference-profile amplitude under sign and spectral conditions. We also prove local constrained existence and uniqueness near a thermal equilibrium with a nonsingular current-beta response and derive a current-pressure bound. An ISTTOK ramp-down example with a prescribed 20% energetic-current fraction and 2 keV energy gives a magnetic-orbit axis separation of 2.39 mm. The resulting fields and current distributions can serve as initial conditions for studies of electron survival and plasma recovery through AC reversal.

papers.title: On stimulated scattering including harmonic generation in an unmagnetized pair plasma for arbitrary pump strengths
papers.abstract: A fully nonlinear analysis for the growth rate of the stimulated backscatter instability of an intense electromagnetic (EM) wave with arbitrary polarization in an unmagnetized pair plasma is presented. The connection of this instability to the FEL process is discussed and utilized. An intense EM wave causes an initially stationary pair plasma to drift forward with a speed near the speed of light. The resulting distribution function for both cold and warm pair plasmas is presented. It is shown that the frequency of the reflected light is thus Doppler downshifted from that of the incident wave. For a linearly polarized EM wave there is also an additional contribution to the forward drift at its second harmonic which leads to backscattered light at all odd harmonics of the Doppler downshifted frequency for sufficiently cold pair plasmas. Fully nonlinear particle-in-cell simulations confirm the theoretical growth rates and show how the instability depends on the pair plasma temperature. The effect of the intensity profile of the incoming EM wave as well as implications for astrophysical pair plasmas is discussed.

papers.title: General Relativistic and Non-Inertial Effects on Magnetic Reconnection Rates
papers.abstract: We develop a gauge-independent theory of magnetic reconnection beyond the standard special-relativistic framework of inertial systems in flat spacetime. Our definitions of reconnection and its rate are independent of reference frame and coordinate system, allowing physical effects of gravity and net linear acceleration to be distinguished from coordinate effects. We extend the mesoscale theory of Liu et al. [PRL 118, 085101 (2017)], in which the reconnection rate depends on physics both within the diffusion region and in an upstream ideal, force-free region. The theory identifies three non-inertial and curved-spacetime (NICS) effects, including gravitationally induced magnetic tension: gravitational distortion of the reconnection plane changes the curvature of magnetic field lines. Applying the theory to a simplified accretion plasma near )a compact object, we find that (1) whether gravity increases or decreases the reconnection rate depends on the system's orientation relative to the gravitational source, with the greatest increase occurring when the outflow jet points toward or away from the source; and (2) the magnitude of the gravitational effect scales with the dimensionless parameter $\bar{\kappa} \equiv r_s\Delta y^2/r^3$, where $r$ is the Schwarzschild radial coordinate, $r_s$ is the source's Schwarzschild radius, and $\Delta y$ is the mesoscale length.

papers.title: Development of Sapphire-Based Solid-State Neutron Detectors for Fusion Environments
papers.abstract: Single-crystal diamond is the reference solid-state technology for fast neutron detection in fusion devices. Despite this, its complex manufacturing increases their costs and puts limitations on their geometry. Moreover, the limits in their long-term stability and their behaviour in harsh environments further constraint its applications. Synthetic sapphire (Al2O2) is a promising alternative as a solid state detector material: it is available in large, low-cost wafers and features both a wider bandgap and a higher displacement energy compared to diamond. Despite this, it has so far received little-to-no attention as a neutron detector. This work presents the first steps of a development programme for sapphire-based fast neutron detectors. Eight prototypes with 4.5 x 4.5 mm2 and 9 x 9 mm2 active areas and 625 um thickness were fabricated from commercial wafers with Al-Si electrodes and coupled to different electronic configurations. All prototypes detected 5.47 MeV alpha particles from a 241Am source, confirming the viability of both the fabrication process and the use of sapphire as an active material. The small signals (30-40 mV over a peak-to-peak noise of about 8 mV) and the count rate increasing with bias indicate that sapphires will require higher electric fields than the ones experimented in the work (up to about 2.5 kV). Geant4 simulations were also used to estimate the response of a sapphire detector to 14.06 MeV (DT) neutrons, highlighting the perspectives of the detector as a fusion diagnostic.

papers.title: Experimental Investigation of Hypersonic Shock-Wave/Boundary-Layer Interaction Dynamics Using Plasma-Generated Disturbances
papers.abstract: The unsteady dynamics of a transitional 3D shock-wave/boundary-layer interaction (SWBLI) are investigated using pulsed plasma disturbances on a cone-slice-ramp geometry in the Boeing/AFOSR Mach-6 Quiet Tunnel. Nanosecond-duration repetitively pulsed spark discharges introduce disturbances which convect through the interaction, causing transient turbulent breakdown in the reattaching shear layer. The unsteady behavior of the separation bubble is characterized using schlieren imaging, and natural broadband unsteadiness is observed in the form of large-scale shock and separation flapping at frequencies below 1500 Hz ($Sr_L< 0.25$). Disturbance packets are introduced at a range of perturbation frequencies and generally induce shear layer oscillations; however, perturbation frequencies below the natural cutoff frequency ($f\approx 1500$ $\mathrm{Hz}$) yield fluctuations with significantly larger amplitudes than those above this frequency. Phase-averaged schlieren images reveal that the disturbances cause a decrease in shear layer height immediately after inducing turbulent breakdown around the reattachment point, with this displacement beginning downstream and moving upstream. The shear layer's response to this displacement is consistent with that of an under-damped dynamic system with a preferred oscillation frequency; the measured frequency of the oscillatory response to external perturbation ($f = 1464$ Hz) is also the approximate cutoff frequency of the natural broadband unsteadiness. Furthermore, the relationship between perturbation frequency and oscillation amplitude resembles that of a low-pass filter, with a cutoff frequency that is within 5\% of the measured oscillator frequency. These experimental findings support the theory that the cutoff frequency for the SWBLI's frequency-selective amplification is tied to the time scale of the weakly damped global mode.

papers.title: Plasma simulations with adaptive mesh and algorithm refinement
papers.abstract: Adaptive Mesh and Algorithm Refinement (AMAR) combines adaptive Cartesian meshes with automatic selection of kinetic or fluid solvers. It was introduced for rarefied gas dynamics and later extended to gas mixtures, particle and lattice-Boltzmann solvers, computational electromagnetics, and multi-phase flows. In weakly ionized plasmas, the species differ by orders of magnitude in mass, velocity, and time scale. This paper describes PAMAR, a plasma extension of AMAR in which electrons, ions, neutral species, and fields can have independent adaptive-mesh solvers, each with its own phase-space dimensionality, refinement criteria, and time step, coupled through a field solver in one executable built on the Basilisk framework. We present two demonstrations. A transient capacitively coupled plasma in argon is simulated with two-stream kinetic solvers for electrons and ions on independent adaptive quadtrees in $(x,v)$. The simulations resolve three electron groups and the time scales of electron and ion kinetics without statistical noise, at a cost between particle-in-cell simulations and fast kinetic models. A sphere at floating potential in a collisionless or weakly collisional plasma is computed with octree solvers in $(r,v,\mu)$ for both species and compared with an exact method-of-characteristics solution. Per-species meshes resolve the cold ions at a tenth of the uniform-mesh cost. Both demonstrations also select the model cell by cell. In the capacitive discharge, a hybrid ion solver is kinetic in the sheaths and fluid in the bulk. Around the sphere, a hybrid electron solver confines the kinetic solver to the loss-cone layer and uses a Fokker-Planck model in position and total energy elsewhere. It conserves particles exactly across the interface and uses 1.6 to 5.3 times fewer cells. We discuss the next steps toward parallel, implicit simulations of higher-dimensional problems.

papers.title: AI4Plasma II: Geometry-Aware Surrogate Modeling for Variable Electrode Gap GEC Plasmas
papers.abstract: Industrial plasma process development requires broad exploration of operating and geometric parameters. Geometric parameters, particularly electrode spacing, affect discharge structure and processing uniformity. Exploring these parameter spaces through repeated high-fidelity simulations can be computationally expensive. Surrogate models can offer rapid predictions, but geometric variation complicates their application because the computational domain and discretization may change across samples. In this work, six geometry-aware surrogate models based on prescribed and learned geometry mappings, extended-domain representation, continuous coordinates, and geometry-native discretizations are compared in terms of their data requirements for accurate predictions of full plasma fields and ion density profiles near the wafer. The simulation dataset spans pressure, voltage, frequency, and electrode gap, with each reference case requiring an average simulation cost of 5.32 CPU h. To achieve a 2% mean error across the four plasma fields, prescribed-mapping Geo-FNO and Transolver require 100 training cases, compared with 250-1000 for the other models. Predicting ion density profiles near the wafer is more demanding and reveals larger differences among models, with prescribed-mapping Geo-FNO requiring the fewest training cases for the profile accuracy targets considered. To further reduce the data required for accurate predictions near the wafer, we introduce charge-separation weighting into the training loss, which reduces the prescribed-mapping Geo-FNO's minimum tested training requirement for a 5% profile error from 1000 to 100 cases. These results support prescribed-mapping Geo-FNO as a practical starting point for the variable-gap problem studied here when a suitable geometry mapping is available, while Transolver achieves the highest prediction accuracy with sufficient training data.

papers.title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
papers.abstract: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 \pi f(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

papers.title: A deterministic theory of kinetic fluctuations in long-range interacting homogeneous systems without collective effects
papers.abstract: Finite-$N$ fluctuations govern the slow relaxation of long-range interacting systems, yet accessing their full statistics demands huge ensembles of costly simulations. We show that, in homogeneous systems without collective effects, this statistical problem collapses onto just three deterministic kinetic equations. Starting from the Landau-Dean-Kawasaki equation, i.e. the stochastic counterpart of the large deviation principle for the Landau equation, we derive the infinite hierarchy of $n$-point moments of the empirical distribution function at leading order in $1/N$. We prove that it is solved exactly by a quasi-Gaussian closure. The resulting minimal Landau fluctuation hierarchy is formed by the Landau equation, a Lyapunov equation for the two-point moment, and a kinetic equation for the three-point moment. From these three equations, all higher-order moments follow algebraically. The hierarchy exactly preserves the collisional invariants and their fluctuations, and predicts the full probability distribution of observables in the central fluctuation regime. Benchmarked against $N$-body realizations, it reproduces the mean, variance and higher-order moments with an accuracy that improves systematically with $N$. A single deterministic time-integration of three coupled partial differential equations thus replaces large ensembles of simulations, for any large $N$.

papers.title: Partition of Unity Data-driven Finite Element Method for Anisotropic Diffusion in Magnetized Plasmas
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation of transport processes in magnetized plasmas is characterized by extreme anisotropy, where diffusion along magnetic field lines can be many orders of magnitude larger than in the perpendicular direction. This anisotropy leads to thin, steep boundary layers and numerical pollution that standard finite element methods struggle to resolve without prohibitive mesh refinement. In this paper, we introduce the Partition of Unity Data-Driven Finite Element Method (PU-DDFEM), a data-driven local model reduction approach, for anisotropic diffusion. The method utilizes a bottom-up construction to enable a complete offline-online splitting. We parametrize the local magnetic field and boundary conditions to generate a snapshot space that captures the essential physics of plasma confinement. Dominant modes are extracted via a local spectral problem to identify representative features. These modes are then mapped to the global domain using a partition of unity to form a conforming approximation space. This ensures that the basis functions are fully reusable across different global magnetic configurations, significantly reducing the online computational overhead for large-scale plasma simulations.
